forecast_results.prediction: Q2 2026 (10 Aug) reports an EPS/EBITDA profit-line beat vs the reset consensus bar
forecast_results.evidence: Emaar reported Q2/H1 2026 results on 2026-08-07 (earlier than the CIQ-estimated ~10 Aug date). Q2 revenue grew 18% YoY but missed analyst expectations by ~6% and fell 7% QoQ. Q2 EBITDA fell 22% QoQ and landed 5% below consensus. Net profit attributable was AED 3.7bn, +9% YoY but -27% QoQ. The falsification_trigger ('Q2 EPS misses consensus OR Q2 EBITDA misses consensus') is satisfied via the EBITDA miss; the confirmation_trigger required BOTH legs to beat, and EBITDA did not. [Investing.com, 'Emaar Properties reports lower profit despite revenue growth', 2026-08-07; Gulf News H1 2026 results summary, 2026-08-07]

forecast_results.prediction: Q2 2026 property pre-sales growth decelerates below Q1-26's +16% YoY
forecast_results.evidence: Property development sales (pre-sales) totaled AED 4.24bn in Q2 2026, DOWN 84% YoY and 81% QoQ -- far below the +16% YoY confirmation_trigger threshold and consistent (cross-checked) with the H1 2026 total property-sales figure of AED 26.6bn (Q1 ~AED 22.3bn implied + Q2 AED 4.24bn ~= AED 26.6bn H1). Total revenue backlog growth also decelerated to +13% YoY (from the +29%/+39% cited in the original decision record), though it remains positive rather than flat. [IndexBox, 'Emaar H1 2026 Results', 2026-08-07; Investing.com Q2 2026 earnings summary, 2026-08-07; Gulf News H1 2026 results, 2026-08-07]

risk_results.risk: Kill criterion 1 -- Q2 2026 pre-sales growth < +16% YoY and falling / backlog growth stepping toward flat (the Dubai cycle turning)
risk_results.evidence: Both legs of this kill criterion are satisfied: pre-sales growth was -84% YoY (and -81% QoQ, i.e. falling further within the same half), and backlog growth decelerated to +13% YoY from the +29%/+39% cited in the original decision record -- a clear step toward flat, though not literally at zero. This is the single most consequential finding of this review window. [IndexBox / Investing.com / Gulf News, all 2026-08-07, cross-checked against the H1 2026 total for internal consistency]

risk_results.risk: Killer risk -- value trap via a value-indifferent Government-of-Dubai controller, compounded by the Dubai cycle rolling over from its 2025 peak
risk_results.evidence: The cyclical leg of the killer risk is now directly evidenced by the Q2 pre-sales collapse and backlog deceleration above. The governance/owner leg (no incentive to crystallize mall value) is reinforced, not newly evidenced, by the AED 200bn Dubai Estate masterplan announcement -- new capital deployment rather than value return to minorities.

risk_results.risk: Kill criterion 2 -- a richly-priced parent asset injected from Dubai Holding, funded by new Emaar shares
risk_results.evidence: The new AED 200bn Dubai Estate masterplan was announced as an Emaar/Dubai Holding-backed development, not disclosed as an asset injection funded by a new Emaar share issuance. No dilutive capital raise found in evidence gathered. Worth monitoring as the masterplan's funding structure becomes clearer.

risk_results.risk: Kill criterion 3 -- development gross margin fades below the guided 'low 50s' toward high-40s
risk_results.evidence: Not directly assessable from evidence gathered -- EBITDA fell 22% QoQ and missed consensus by 5%, which is suggestive but is not the specific development gross-margin metric named in the kill criterion. Not assessable this review.

risk_results.risk: Kill criterion 5 -- net cash swings to material net debt via a debt-funded capital call
risk_results.evidence: No evidence of a debt-funded capital call found. H1 2026 EBITDA and net profit before tax both grew double digits YoY, consistent with continued self-funding.

risk_results.risk: Kill criterion 6 -- founder-MD (Alabbar) departs abruptly, or Emaar<->Eagle Hills deal-flow diversion evidence surfaces
risk_results.evidence: Alabbar remained visibly active in the period (quoted commentary on H1 2026 results and the new masterplan). No deal-flow diversion evidence found.

lessons: The engine's own named forward test fired within the 30-day window, in the direction the caution anticipated: kill criterion 1 (Q2 pre-sales growth < +16% YoY and falling, backlog growth stepping toward flat) is satisfied -- pre-sales fell 84% YoY, and backlog growth decelerated from +29%/+39% to +13% YoY. This is the specific, dated, falsifiable evidence the record's edge_proof said would disprove the priced-in FCF collapse if it held above +16%; it did not hold, and the record's caution is validated rather than contradicted.

Price outcome: entry AED 12.20 (2026-06-28, CIQ-derived, 12 days stale at decision time) to AED 11.50 (2026-08-07 close) = -5.74%, against a DFM General Index move of approximately -0.63% over a closely-matched window (5,955.58 on 2026-06-30 to 5,918 on 2026-08-06) = -5.11pp benchmark-relative. As a Watchlist with no position, this is opportunity cost AVOIDED, not loss -- the record explicitly declined to recommend a starter long unless pre-sales held >=+16% YoY, and pre-sales missed that bar by a wide margin. The engine's discipline not to upgrade is what a Watchlist call is supposed to do when the risk it names actually shows up.

decision_quality is scored 'skill' on this basis: the specific, falsifiable, dated threshold (pre-sales >=+16% YoY) that would have justified moving off Watchlist toward a starter long was missed by ~100 percentage points, and price moved down rather than toward the base-case AED 15.00 target -- both the analytical call (cycle-peak risk is real) and the position discipline (do not buy) are validated by the same evidence. This should not be read as a call to become more bearish than Watchlist; the wholly-owned mall-annuity value argument (~79% of EV) is unaffected by this print and was never the part of the thesis being tested here.

New forward-looking item not previously in the thesis: Emaar and Dubai Holding unveiled a ~AED 200bn ('Dubai Estate') masterplan for 150,000 residents during this window. This is a large NEW capital commitment layered on top of a quarter where pre-sales just collapsed 84% YoY -- worth watching as a capital-discipline question (financing structure, dilution risk, pace of deployment) even though no dilutive raise or asset-injection-from-parent structure has been disclosed yet.

PROCESS NOTE, judged only on information available on or before 2026-07-10 (no hindsight): the record's own kill_criteria list and edge_proof pre-specified this exact test (a +16% YoY pre-sales threshold) before the print, and the print resolved cleanly against the bullish case. This is the outcome the CLAUDE.md Section 24 Rejector Doctrine is written to reward -- avoiding a value trap is a valid result, not a missed opportunity, when the avoided upside (AED 15.00 base case, +22.95%) did not in fact materialize and the price instead fell.

Single most important takeaway: the Watchlist rating and the specific, dated kill criterion attached to it both did their job in 30 days. The remaining open question is unchanged from the original thesis -- whether a minority-friendly owner action ever crystallizes the mall-annuity value -- and this review found no evidence either way on that question; if anything, the new AED 200bn masterplan is a mild negative signal for near-term crystallization, since it commits capital to new development rather than to shareholder returns.

memo_delta.summary: Emaar reported Q2/H1 2026 results on 2026-08-07, ahead of the CIQ-estimated ~10 Aug date. Property pre-sales collapsed 84% YoY (81% QoQ) to AED 4.24bn, EBITDA fell 22% QoQ and missed consensus by 5%, and backlog growth decelerated to +13% YoY from the +29%/+39% cited in the original decision. This is exactly the kill criterion (pre-sales <+16% YoY and falling, backlog stepping toward flat) the record wrote as its near-term Dubai-cycle test, and it fired. Separately, Emaar and Dubai Holding unveiled a new ~AED 200bn masterplan -- a large new capital commitment, not a value-crystallizing action for minorities. The price fell from AED 12.20 to AED 11.50 (-5.74%, -5.11pp vs the DFM General Index) over the same window. The Watchlist rating and the caution behind it are confirmed, not weakened.

memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Emaar's Q2 2026 print, reported 7 August, confirmed the exact risk we flagged as our reason to stay on the sidelines. We wrote a specific test in July: if pre-sales held above 16 percent year on year growth, the priced-in earnings collapse would be disproven; if not, the Dubai cycle was turning. Pre-sales fell 84 percent year on year instead, and EBITDA missed consensus by 5 percent. This is not a surprise that hurts us -- it is the risk we declined to bet against. We took no position, and the shares fell from 12.20 to 11.50 dirhams, about 5.7 percent, roughly 5 points worse than the Dubai market index over the same stretch. Separately, Emaar and its state parent unveiled a new 200 billion dirham development plan, which commits fresh capital rather than returning the trapped mall value to minority holders -- a mild negative for the part of our thesis that depends on the owner eventually acting differently. We are keeping the Watchlist rating. The mall-annuity value argument is untouched by this print; what changed is confirmation that the cyclical risk gating it is real and already showing up in the numbers.
